notes.0-2: 'rear' also means lift or set upright: 'the horse raised/reared its head', 'raised a monument' = erected
notes.0-3: 'raised the bar' / 'raised the shelf' reads as lifted physically or increased the level
notes.1-3: 'the report raised concerns about safety' = brought them up or heightened them
notes.3-4: 'the drive raised the fund by $500' / 'raised another $5,000' = collected or increased the total

notes.0-2: sales pitch is a live baseball metaphor: 'he threw his best pitch and it missed' / 'his pitch fell flat' supports either
notes.2-3: 'she adjusted her pitch for the older audience' = her persuasive spiel or her voice tone

notes.0-4: 'he changed his pitch for the investors' = tone of voice or persuasive speech
notes.1-2: cricket: 'that was a fast pitch' / 'the pitch was lively' = the playing strip or the delivery
notes.1-3: 'the pitch was too steep for a match' reads as the sloping field or its slope
notes.2-4: 'his opening pitch went wide' = a thrown ball or a persuasive speech (baseball metaphor)

notes.1-2: 'across the lake we could see the bank rising above the water' = a fog/cloud bank or the shore
notes.1-3: 'a bank of clouds along the horizon' = a mass of cloud or a row of them
